name: Bahrain
headline: Bahrain: +3.5% growth in 2025, −0.1% inflation, debt 144% of GDP
sections: Bahrain is a $49.0 billion economy (2025), the world's 100th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +3.5% in 2025, close to the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $71K at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 19.9% of GDP (2025).
Consumer prices rose −0.1% in 2025, in deflation, down from 3.6% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 5.6% (2025), above the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 5.4% (2025).
Gross government debt is 144% of GDP (2025), a very high level that has risen from 126% in 2020. The general government balance is −13.2% of GDP (2025), a deficit beyond the common 3% benchmark.
The current account balance is +5.0% of GDP (2025), a large surplus. Trade equals 157% of GDP (2024), a highly open economy. Net FDI inflows were 1.7% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 162% of GDP by 2031, still rising from today's level. Life expectancy is 81.4 years (2024). Population: 1.6 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
